Preprocessing, feature selection, and model performance evaluation are all used in the suggested method. The DWT method is used for preprocessing in the suggested method. PCA and LDA are used for feature selection. The suggested method employs ResNet LS TM to assess the efficiency of the model. Two conventional approaches, LSTM and GRU, are contrasted with the proposed methodology. The proposed method outperforms the other two.

articleTitle: ECMS: Implementation of System Design to Evaluate the Data Transmission Efficiency Over Vehicular AdHoc Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: In order to aid in autonomous driving, lessen traffic on networks, and deal with road accidents of any sort, Vehicular Ad-hoc Networks (VANETs) are being utilized in a wide range of intelligent transport technologies. This research focuses on safety applications in which cars transmit safety warnings that are both time-sensitive and reliant on a constant connection. Taking on this study was motivated by the necessity of promptly and reliably disseminating VANET safety warnings broadcast throughout the network. The rapid mobility of cars in VANET causes the connection between nodes to often drop. Broadcasting messages in a vehicle ad hoc network is thus still an unanswered research question that requires more study to resolve optimally. This study solves this issue by creating an Optimum Distance Routing Model (ODRM). This study suggests a novel architecture for VANET that is adaptable, straightforward, and extensible, as well as a novel protocol for broadcasting, both of which improve the pace at which packets are received and which use less bandwidth. The analytical model has established criteria for selecting the optimal vehicle to serve as the cluster head node, and simulation tests have compared the new technique to existing alternatives. The simulation tests have shown that the suggested RVC approach is superior to the present techniques in terms of increasing the likelihood of packet error recovery and the rate at which packets are delivered.

articleTitle: Tomato Leaf Disease Detection using Feature Extraction and Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Tomatoes, as one of the most significant fruits, play an important role in Indian cuisine due to their nutritional value and other elements such as antioxidants. With a good climate and appropriate rainfall, the tomato plant generates the highest output, and India is second only to China in tomato production. Tomatoes are recognized as both a commercial and a nutritious crop that contributes to the nation's economy. Though tomatoes can be cultivated all year, obstacles such as heavy rains, temperature swings, fertilizer levels, and moisture stages cause production issues. Diseases caused by fungi, bacteria, and viruses damage the plant and ruin the fruit, causing farmers to lose a lot of money. The infections are detectable in the early stage is avoided by the appearance of the leaves, but it is difficult for human vision. As a result, computer-aided processes are used to identify normal and a typical plant using Machine and deep learning algorithms. This research proposes easy approaches for detecting illnesses in tomato plants by classifying leaves to determine whether it belong to a healthy plant. To extract the best attributes for categorization, feature extraction methods are used. For classification, Random Forest outperforms all other models with 86% accuracy.

articleTitle: An Innovative Method for Snatch Theft Detection Using Convolutional LSTM-Auto Encoder Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Urban areas frequently experience snatch stealing, a severe threat to public safety. It entails forcibly seizing a victim's personal items, including purses or cell phones, before scurrying away from the scene. Due to how quickly they happen, it is difficult to identify snatch theft instances in real-time. The systems now in use to identify the snatching occurrences mainly rely on human participation, which may result in lengthy delays and mistakes. Consequently, there is a need for an automated method that can quickly and effectively identify these situations. Preprocessing, segmentation, feature extraction, and model training are all used in the suggested method. Gaussian Model is utilized for preprocessing. Canny edge is utilized for segmentation. LSTM-AE is used to train the model. Two further models, LSTM and AE, are contrasted with the suggested method. When compared to two existing approaches, the proposed strategy performs exceptionally well.

articleTitle: Predicting the Likelihood of Type2 Diabetes with Random Forest Classifier
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: A chronic medical illness known as diabetes is defined by elevated levels of the body's natural sugar, or glucose, in the blood. Over time, numerous researchers have endeavored to establish dependable diabetes prediction models. However, the field continues to grapple with unresolved research challenges due to insufficient data sets and prediction methods. Consequently, researchers are compelled to employ machine learning and big data analytics methodologies to address these issues. This research study has analyzed two widely recognized classification models, namely Decision Tree and Logistic Regression. Further, this research study has investigated the Bagging and Boosting methods to increase the toughness of these models. Additionally, the assessment of Random Forest is considered as a part of the research investigation. The results indicate that the Random Forest algorithm yielded the most promising performance in classifying the disease risk.

articleTitle: R-LSTM-CNN Framework Based Lung Cancer Detection and Classification from Chest CT Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Lung cancer is one of the top causes of death worldwide, accounting for almost five million lives lost annually. Computed Tomography (CT) scan findings can be used to help diagnose lung conditions. The fundamental objective of this work is to detect malignant nodules in the lungs and classify the severity of lung cancer based on an input lung image. In this proposed approach to use state-of-the-art Deep learning techniques to precisely locate cancerous lung nodules. Preprocessing, segmentation, feature extraction, and model training are the first four steps of the proposed method. The major goal of this preprocessing is to extract the lung area from the CT scan image, along with any other ROIs that may be present. A huge digital image can be broken down into more manageable chunks using a process called segmentation. Intensity and gradient orientation histograms, as well as Gabor and entropy filters, are used in feature extraction. After leveraging information gain to choose useful features, the models are trained via R-LSTM-CNN. The proposed method outperforms the two most popular competing methods, CNN and LSTM.

articleTitle: Advancing Music Genre Identification Through Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Music plays a huge role in human's lives, inspiring a wide range of feelings including enthusiasm and nostalgia. 97 million songs have been recorded globally; an incredible figure that is only increasing exponentially as more people use music applications. Many people love particular musical genres, such as classical, hip-hop, or disco, and want for an easy way to arrange their music in accordance with their preferences. This gave rise to the idea of “music genre classification”. In the current environment, where there are many music recordings available both online and offline, proper genre categorization has become essential. Several machine learning methods may be used to categorize the different types of music. This model's emphasis is on using deep learning methods to identify the musical genre. The Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC), a technique that works exceptionally well for music files, are used to extract key elements. The proposed model is excellent at categorizing musical subgenres and provides default settings as well as interactive options depending on user preferences. The simple web interface built using Flask allows users to submit audio files and view the anticipated genre. The system also has the capability of recommending new genres to the user.

articleTitle: Hybrid Task Cascade Region-Based Convolutional Neural Network is Used to Analyse Cricket Scores
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Cricket scorecards reflect both teams' batting and bowling statistics. It usually contains each team's runs, wickets, and overs, as well as each batter's strike rate and bowler's data. The scoreboard also lists extras like wides, no-balls and wickets. Players, coaches, and analysts need a cricket scorecard to analyse performance, identify strengths and shortcomings, and make strategic choices. The Hybrid Task Cascade regions-Based convolutional neural networks (HTC-RCNN) is a computer vision model for object detection and instance segmentation. This novel design blends Cascade and Mask Region-based Convolutional Neural Networks (Mask R-CNN) models. Cricket scorecards are evaluated using Hybrid Task Cascade regions with convolutional neural networks. Cricket scorecards include each player's runs, wickets, and other statistics. Cricket scorecards may be automatically extracted and evaluated using the Hybrid Task Cascade regions with a convolutional neural networks model. Hybrid Task Cascade regions with convolutional neural networks multi-stage cascade design accurately identifies and segments objects. The model can detect and classify player names, runs scored, wickets were taken, batting and bowling statistics, and other significant cricket scorecard components. The Hybrid Task Cascade regions with convolutional neural networks model can automate the retrieval of important cricket scoreboard data, saving time and effort. This automatic analysis may help cricket match summaries, player evaluations, and statistical insights. Post-processing refines and verifies extracted data. According to experiments, the suggested technique beats current approaches in accuracy and efficiency. The suggested method correctly identifies team, player, and run names at 96.1%, 98.7%, and 97.3%, respectively.

Author Keywords: Hybrid Task Cascade Region-Based Convolutional Neural Network

articleTitle: Retinal Vessel Classification and Segmentation Using Advanced Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The automated segmentation of blood vessels in retinal fundus images plays a critical role in the field of medical imaging analysis. To create a decision support system to help in the initial diagnosis and treatment of retinal sickness, precise vascular segmentation is regarded to be crucial. Using fuzzy edge detection and learning approaches, this research creates a system that can segment and classify retinal blood vessels. To begin, the proposed RBVSC-FEDLM model employs a contrast enhancement method. In addition to employing GOA to fine-tune the membership functions, a Fuzzy Cluster Network Algorithm for Edge Detection (FCNAED) technique is employed to locate the edges of retinal fundus images. The ORB (Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF) feature extractor is used for the extraction of feature vectors. Finally, the use of Auto Encoder (AE) for categorizing retinal images is a novel contribution to the field. This study uses a benchmark dataset to verify the RBVSC-FEDLM model's accuracy, and found that it outperforms state-of-the-art alternatives.

articleTitle: Enhancing Profanity Detection in Textual Data Using Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The proliferation of offensive language and content, often referred to as 'profanity,’ poses significant challenges across various digital platforms. Profanity detection in textual data plays a crucial rolein various domains such as social media monitoring, online content moderation, and cyberbullying prevention. This approach aims to enhance profanity detection in textual data using Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks to prevent offensive content. The performance of profanity detection is improved in this work by utilizing a novel approach that makes use of cutting-edge deep learning techniques. To be more precise, This approach uses a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory network, a powerful deep learning architecture for sequence classification, to model the intricate relationships between words in textual data. Furthermore, this incorporates fine-tuned pre-trained word embeddings to capture semantic information and contextual cues, thereby augmenting the performance of the model. Through extensive experimentation and evaluation of exemplary datasets, the approach achieves a remarkable accuracy rate of 88.3%. Modern methodologies are outperformed by the suggested approach in terms of memory, accuracy, recall, and precision. The efficiency of the method opens up avenues for its application in real-world scenarios, facilitating more effective social media monitoring, online content moderation, and proactive cyberbullying prevention. The findings contribute to advancing the field of profanity detection and hold promise for future research in this domain.

articleTitle: Design and Development of an Intelligent Number Plate Identification System Utilizing Raspberry Pi Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: In many parts of the world, traffic law violations are a significant contributor to road accidents, particularly in developing countries. Despite the existence of rules and regulations to prevent such violations, the number of violators continues to rise due to inadequate enforcement by authorities in these regions. To enhance road safety and reduce accidents, a system must be developed to aid law enforcement agencies in enforcing these rules. The primary objective of this article is to use image processing to detect traffic violators by their number plates. The system comprises an IR sensor for detecting vehicles, which is connected to a microprocessor that records the time taken for the sensor to detect an object. When the time taken is below the minimum threshold, the camera captures the plate number, and the image is stored on a Raspberry Pi 4 for processing. OpenALPR dataset is selected for the proposed work. The Raspberry Pi 4 extracts the numbers from the image. Accuracy, time complexity, and cost are calculated for the proposed work to measure its performance. It is also compared with some states of artwork for its validation. Implementation of the proposed system can enhance road safety and traffic control in developing smart cities. Top of Form

articleTitle: Analysis of Discovering Fraud in Master Card Based on Bidirectional GRU and CNN Based Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: Detecting and confirming MasterCard fraud (also known as “master card fraud detection”) is a popular course topic amongst students due to the usefulness of data processing and machine learning strategies in combating cybercrime. The three main parts of the proposed method are preprocessing, feature extraction, and model training. Preprocessing techniques are used to mine crucial information for identifying MasterCard fraud. Only by using the most advanced and efficient algorithms, the future transactions can be predicted with any degree of certainty. By employing these techniques, the proposed approach may confirm a variety of facts, including the correctness of authentication and the regularity of dealings. To accomplish feature extraction, the proposed approach used the PCA and SKM algorithms. In order to train the models following feature extraction, the proposed approach uses CNN, BiGRU, and BiGRU-CNN. Both the CNN and the BiGRU models are outperformed by the proposed model. With an approximate 98.87 percent accuracy, the proposed method is superior to other methods such as CNN and BiGRU.

articleTitle: An Evaluation of Machine Learning Techniques for Detecting Banking Frauds

abstract: Credit cards are an essential part of every person's daily life in the modern world. Customers use their credit cards and online transactions to make purchases for their requirements. articleTitle: To Improving the Performance of Identification and Segregation of Liquid and Solid from Municipal Waste Using Adam Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Self Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Systems (ICSSAS)
abstract: The identification and segregation of liquid and solid waste for efficient recycling can be enhanced through the application of machine learning algorithms. Waste management plays a crucial role in minimizing environmental impact and promoting sustainable practices. The use of machine learning algorithms to optimize waste identification and segregation processes, leading to efficient recycling practices. Algorithms offer a promising approach to automate and streamline the waste management process. This algorithm can be trained on large datasets comprising various waste samples to learn patterns and characteristics that distinguish liquid and solid waste. By utilizing features such as color, texture, and composition, machine learning models can accurately classify waste streams, even in complex scenarios. Once waste is accurately identified, machine learning algorithms can aid in the segregation process. By analyzing the physical and chemical properties of waste samples, this ADAM algorithms can determine the appropriate separation methods for liquid and solid waste streams. This targeted segregation approach reduces contamination and enhances the quality of recyclable materials. Efficient recycling practices bring numerous benefits, including reduced resource consumption, energy conservation, and minimized pollution. By leveraging machine learning algorithms, waste management systems can achieve higher levels of accuracy and precision, leading to improved recycling outcomes. Additionally, the automation of waste identification and segregation processes can enhance operational efficiency
